source_text: Floor levels of habitable rooms must be a minimum of 0.5m above the 1% AEP flood level at that location. For areas of minor overland flow (a flood depth of 300mm or less or overland flow of 2cum/sec or less) a lower freeboard of 300mm may be considered on its merits.
condition: Applies to floor levels of habitable rooms in new residential development; a lower freeboard of 300mm may be considered on its merits for areas of minor overland flow (flood depth 300mm or less, or overland flow 2 cum/sec or less).
review_note: NEW, and the cleanest freeboard in the set. 'Floor levels of habitable rooms must be a minimum of 0.5m above the 1% AEP flood level at that location.' DIRECTION is handled correctly: the 300mm minor-overland-flow concession is in the condition, not in value_min, so a consumer gets the requirement rather than the concession. LGA-wide, mandatory wording, and measured above the 1% AEP -- the standard datum the other accepted rows use.

source_text:
9.8 Habitable floor levels of all residential and institutional buildings are to be a minimum
of 0.5m above the 1 in 100-year flood level.
condition: Applies to habitable floor levels of residential and institutional buildings on sites affected by 1-in-100-year (mainstream) flooding (general overland flow / drainage provisions, Section 9).
review_note: NEW, and this is Canterbury-Bankstown's general answer: '9.8 Habitable floor levels of all residential and institutional buildings are to be a minimum of 0.5m above the 1 in 100-year flood level.' Mandatory wording, LGA-wide, measured above the 1-in-100-year level. 'all residential and institutional' is why universal_residential is the right dev_type rather than a single dwelling class.

source_text:
3 Where the design flood standard is less than 20m3/s, or identified as
overland flow on the Flood Planning Area Map* the minimum floor
level of all enclosed areas and structures, including all habitable floor
areas, is to be either:
i) 300mm above the design flood standard level; or
ii) 300mm above the highest existing ground level along the
associated overland flow path; or
iii) whichever is the greater, except in the case of garages, where
the minimum height is to be 150mm instead of 300mm, and in-
ground swimming pools, which is to be designed in accordance
with the provisions of 24D.7 (4) of this Part
condition: ONLY WHERE the design flood standard is LESS THAN 20m3/s, or the land is identified as overland flow on the Flood Planning Area Map. Minimum floor level of all enclosed areas and structures, including habitable floor areas, is 300mm above the design flood standard level. See the paired 500mm control for mainstream flow.
review_note: NEW, and one of a genuine PAIR: Ku-ring-gai sets the freeboard by flow regime, 300mm below 20 cubic metres per second and 500mm above it. Both rows are needed or the LGA has no answer for half its flood-affected land, and neither can be served without its test, so the flow-regime condition is moved to the front. This is a conditional control, not an ambiguous one: the document states the test, it is not being inferred.

4 Where the design flood standard exceeds 20m3/s, or as identified
as mainstream flow on the Flood Planning Area Map* the minimum
floor level for all enclosed areas, including all habitable floor areas,
are to be 500mm above the design flood standard level, except in
the case of garages, where the minimum height is to be 300mm, and
in- ground swimming pools, which is to be designed in accordance
with the provisions of 24D.7 (3,4,5) of this Part.
condition: ONLY WHERE the design flood standard EXCEEDS 20m3/s, or the land is identified as mainstream flow on the Flood Planning Area Map. Minimum floor level for all enclosed areas, including habitable floor areas, is 500mm above the design flood standard level; garages carry a reduced figure. See the paired 300mm control for overland flow.

Both rows are needed or the LGA has no answer for half its flood-affected land, and neither can be served without its test, so the flow-regime condition is moved to the front. This is a conditional control, not an ambiguous one: the document states the test, it is not being inferred.

C5 Floor Levels (Flood Planning Levels) Of Habitable Rooms Must Be A
# 2.22 Flood Management — C5 Floor Levels (Flood Planning Levels) Of Habitable Rooms Must Be A

minimum of 500mm above the 1% AEP flood level at that location.
condition: Floor levels (Flood Planning Levels) of habitable rooms, 500mm above the 1% AEP flood level at that location. For areas of minor overland flow (a depth of 300mm or less, or overland flow of 2 cubic metres per second or less) a lower freeboard of 300mm may be considered on its merits.
review_note: NEW, and the QUOTE was not evidence as proposed. The extraction split this clause: its subject sits in the section header ('C5 Floor Levels (Flood Planning Levels) Of Habitable Rooms Must Be A') and only the predicate ('minimum of 500mm above the 1% AEP flood level at that location') reached source_text. Read alone, the proposed quote never says WHAT must be 500mm above anything -- a reviewer could not check it. Corrected to the contiguous span that carries both halves, sliced from the page rather than retyped, and re-verified. No number changed. Substantively this is the same clause as Ashfield's DS2.1, including the identical 300mm minor-overland-flow concession, which is what two former Inner West councils sharing a drafting lineage looks like.
